Container.Name: rea-mcp
Container.Overview: A remote MCP server for reverse engineering. It serves REA (rea-agents) with Ghidra, tshark and objdump over HTTP, so Claude (a custom connector) and Claude Code can analyze files in the folder you mount at /samples. Every request needs the API key you set below, and the server will not start without a key of at least 32 characters. The container speaks plain HTTP: put it behind TLS, for example a Cloudflare Tunnel, before exposing it. It has no web page. The agent can be handed a file with a one-time upload URL, and reads large results in pieces. Each session runs its own REA and Ghidra process, so size MAX_SESSIONS and GHIDRA_MAX_HEAP against your RAM. Only analyze software you are permitted to analyze.

Config.Name: Port
Config.Description: Port the MCP endpoint (/mcp) and the health check (/healthz) listen on.

Config.Name: API key
Config.Description: Required. A long random key, at least 32 characters, that clients send in the x-api-key header. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. There is no default and the container will not start without one.

Config.Name: Samples (read-only)
Config.Description: Required. A dedicated folder that holds only the files you may analyze. It is mounted read-only; do not mount a share that holds anything else.

Config.Name: Work directory
Config.Description: Where Ghidra output, per-session folders and the optional checkpoint folder go. It must be writable by uid 99, gid 100 (nobody:users), which the container runs as.

Config.Name: Max sessions
Config.Description: Most sessions that can be open at once. Each has its own REA and Ghidra process; a request over the limit gets 503.

Config.Name: Session idle timeout (s)
Config.Description: Seconds without any request after which an idle session is ended. Claude Code does not end its sessions when a conversation finishes, so this is how long a finished conversation keeps its slot and its Ghidra. A conversation that is quiet for longer loses its open binary. A call that is still running is never counted as idle.

Config.Name: Trust proxy
Config.Description: Set to true only behind a trusted proxy such as a Cloudflare Tunnel, so the client address is read from CF-Connecting-IP or X-Forwarded-For for the failed-login limit. Leave false when clients reach the container directly.

Config.Name: Allowed hosts
Config.Description: Comma-separated host names accepted in the Host header of /mcp requests and of upload and download URLs, for example the tunnel's host name. Empty accepts any host. The health check is exempt.

Config.Name: Public base URL
Config.Description: The address the agent's curl uses to reach this container, used to build the one-time upload and download URLs the agent is given: an http or https address with a host name (and a port if needed) and nothing else, no path. Set it when the container is behind a TLS proxy such as a Cloudflare Tunnel; empty builds the URL from the request's Host header with http, which a proxy that redirects http to https will break. It is a host name, not a secret.

Config.Name: Max upload (bytes)
Config.Description: Largest single file the agent may upload, in bytes (default 256 MiB). A proxy in front may have a lower limit of its own: a Cloudflare Tunnel passes at most 100 MiB (104857600) per request on the Free and Pro plans.

Config.Name: Inbox size limit (bytes)
Config.Description: Most that the inbox (the inbox folder in the work directory, where uploaded files are kept) may hold, in bytes, counting uploads in progress (default 4 GiB). Nothing deletes files from it: clear it yourself when it is full.

Config.Name: Upload and download URL lifetime (s)
Config.Description: Seconds an unused one-time upload or download URL stays valid.

Config.Name: Largest inline result (characters)
Config.Description: A tool result longer than this (as serialized JSON) is stored in the work directory and replaced by a short preview the agent pages through, so a client is never sent more than it will take. 0 turns this off, and results and tool schemas are then passed on exactly as REA sent them. Otherwise 2000 to 10000000.

Config.Name: Ghidra max heap
Config.Description: Maximum Java heap of each Ghidra process, for example 4G or 512M. Empty uses REA's default of 2G. Memory use is roughly Max sessions times this, plus overhead for each session.

Config.Name: Ghidra startup timeout (ms)
Config.Description: Milliseconds Ghidra may take to start before REA gives up. Empty uses REA's default of 330000 (5.5 minutes).

Config.Name: Ghidra checkpoint directory
Config.Description: Off while empty. Set to /work/checkpoints to keep Ghidra's analysis of each binary across sessions and restarts. Read first: names and comments saved in one conversation appear in any later one that opens the same binary; only one live session can hold a given binary; targets that are not stock ELF, PE or Mach-O imports fail to open with Ghidra; nothing is ever deleted from it. Stopping a session is then given 30 seconds, so raise unRAID's Docker Stop Timeout (Settings, Docker) to at least 40 seconds, or REA may be killed while saving.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: One of debug, info, warn or error. Logs never contain request headers or keys at any level.
